newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold easier, seasonal demand sustained.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold easier, seasonal demand sustained.

text.p: Traded volume on the Istanbul gold exchange slipped to 1,542 kilos on Thursday from Wednesday's 1,893 kilos with trade dominated by sustained seasonal physical demand, dealers said.
Gold closed easier at $323.00 an ounce and 1,637,500 lira per gram, compared to $325.20 and 1,648,000 lira on Wednesday, following lower levels on European markets.

"There is a lot of physical demand on the market right now plus a slight shortage of gold which is holding prices higher than they otherwise would be until the banks import more, probably after the weekend," one dealer said.
Demand for gold in Turkey usually rises in the summer months with the increased number of weddings and other festivals.
The Turkish lira fell to 157,530 to the dollar from Wednesday's close of 157,300 easing gold's fall in lira terms.
Almost all the day's trade -- 1,462 kilos -- took place in the morning session, with 58.0 percent conducted in lira terms. --Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875
